args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Actions taken: (1) Attempted rollback to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy, but it was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined for CVE-2026-4417. (2) Rolled back to v2.2.9, the next most recent production release that was healthy. Rollout verified in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), and the service is now healthy with error rate 0.002. Follow-ups: v2.3.1 remains unhealthy and should not be redeployed until fixed. v2.3.0 is quarantined, so the team needs to decide on a fix path for the CVE and whether v2.2.9 stays as the production version.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.2.9 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service is healthy again with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.

- **Target version:** The most recent healthy production release was v2.3.0. The rollback to it was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined for CVE-2026-4417. Nothing changed from that attempt.
- **Fallback:** The next most recent healthy production release was v2.2.9, so I rolled back to it. This was a rollback to a version that had already run healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failed v2.3.0 attempt, the v2.2.9 rollback, and the verified recovery.

Follow-ups for the team:
- v2.3.1 is still unhealthy and should not be redeployed until it is fixed.
- Because v2.3.0 is quarantined, the team needs to decide how to handle the CVE and whether v2.2.9 stays as the production version.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 (seq 3) is unhealthy and is running in all three regions. I'll roll back to v2.3.0.
v2.3.0 is quarantined for CVE-2026-4417, so the service rejected that rollback and nothing changed. The next most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.2.9, so I'll try that.
